messages:
maya: heads-up — saw a regression this morning: cross-region requests hitting eu-west1 that fall back to us-central are showing a ~30% increase in P95 token latency. KV cache miss rate for /generate-chat jumped from ~4% -> ~18% around 03:12 UTC. attaching quick notes below.

liam: do we know if this is kernel selection related or batching heuristics?

olivia: initial profile looks like kernel selection + memcpy overhead. for long sequences (>1024) the selector appears to pick the generic attention kernel instead of the optimized int8_fused kernel, so per-token attention time doubles. also noticed batch sizes dropped on the route (p50 batch_size 4 -> 2) which increases tail.

maya: repro steps i used: replay traffic from 03:10-03:20 (eu-west1) at production rate with route tag /generate-chat and region routing rules. profiler flamegraph saved as link: https://redwood-internal/prof/174820

liam: sample perf counters from the run:
```
rdruntime_kernel_choice_total{region="eu-west1",route="/generate-chat",kernel="int8_fused"} 24
rdruntime_kernel_choice_total{region="eu-west1",route="/generate-chat",kernel="generic_attn"} 178
rdruntime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.02"} 120000
rdruntime_kvcache_hit_ratio{region="eu-west1",route="/generate-chat"} 0.82
rdruntime_batch_size_histogram{route="/generate-chat"} 2 5 6 3 1
```

olivia: my suspicion: recent change to batching heuristics (PR 2026-03-15) made the runtime conservative for multi-region routes to avoid cross-region batching that previously caused lock-step spikes. it reduced batching window to 8ms for those routes. that helped some tail in other cases but hurt throughput here because kv-cache prefix reuse needed slightly larger batches to amortize memcpy cost.

maya: idea: add token-level breakdown panels (tokenize, attention_kernel, memcpy_kv, kv_lookup, postproc). need these per-route and per-region so we can see which step dominates on failover. example PromQLs below.

liam: agreed. rough PromQLs:
```
# P95 token latency per component
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(rdruntime_token_component_seconds_bucket{component!=""}[5m])) by (le,component,route,region))

# KV cache hit ratio by route
sum(rate(rdruntime_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (route,region) / sum(rate(rdruntime_kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (route,region)

# kernel selection distribution
sum(rate(rdruntime_kernel_choice_total[5m])) by (kernel,route,region)
```

sara-oncall: can we also surface cross-region failover rate metric? something like ratio of requests served from non-primary region when routing_policy != primary. that would help correlate spikes with failover events.

olivia: yes — propose derived metric: rdruntime_failover_rate{route,region} = failover_count(route,region) / requests(route,region). We can emit failover_count from the routing layer when a request is routed to fallback region.

maya: quick dashboard plan: 1) Token-level waterfall (stacked bars) per route/region, 2) Kernel selector heatmap, 3) KV cache hit ratio trend with prefix-length bucket, 4) Cross-region failover rate + per-route P95 token latency overlay.

liam: note on implementation — kernel selector currently only logs choice in debug. we'll add a low-cost counter with labels {kernel,arch,seq_len_bucket,route,region} and ensure it samples at request completion. keep cardinality bounded by using seq_len_bucket.

olivia: also instrument memcpy bytes/time between device->host for kvcache fallback path. most of the spike on long seqs looks like memcpy + attention kernel fallback.

maya: temporary mitigation: revert the batching-window change for multi-region routes or add route-level override (we can flip feature flag). patch to toggle below:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api/featureflags/runtime-batching -d '{"route": "/generate-chat", "window_ms": 16}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/runtime-batching-override -> canary (3 nodes)

liam: follow-ups:
- liam: add kernel choice counters + memcpy timers (PR queued)
- olivia: add token-component histogram + Grafana panels (dashboard PR)
- maya: emit failover_count from router and add alert when failover_rate > 0.05 for >10m

sara-oncall: scheduling oncall handoff to verify after canary, i'll watch the dashboard and lean on alerts. :eyes:

maya: thanks all. i'll capture the flamegraph and rough root-cause notes in the incident thread if it worsens. for now i'll leave the canary running and watch p95 token latency by region/route. :thumbsup:
